title: Two upgrades worth the marks
one: Two things a case study can ask for that the bike shop did not need, each a small step on from code you know.
marks: A project that copies the bike shop well earns good marks. The top marks go to a project that also handles something the bike shop did not need, built with the same rules.

stages.title: Why these two upgrades earn marks

screens.title: Read why these two upgrades earn marks.

blocks.p: A project that copies the bike shop's shapes well earns good marks. The top marks go to a project that also handles something the bike shop did not need. Many case studies have one of the two things below, and each one is a small step on from code you already know.

box.title: Upgrade one: one supplier order with many lines
box.text: In the bike shop, one order is for one part. A real supplier order often holds tyres, chains and brake pads on the same piece of paper. That needs a header table for the order and a line table for each thing on it, and the stored procedure that receives the delivery must put up the stock of every line at once.

box.title: Upgrade two: a booking held for a short time, then let go
box.text: A customer who books a service but has not paid the deposit yet has a booking that is held, but only until a deadline. That needs a status called Provisional, a column that holds the deadline, and a stored procedure that cancels every held booking whose deadline has passed.

blocks.p: Both upgrades are code blocks to read, not to copy. Read them here, part by part. Do not paste them into your BikeShop script, because the bike shop does not need them. If your case study needs one, build it in your own project, with your own names, using the method in chapter 11.

stages.title: Upgrade one: one order with many lines

screens.title: Read upgrade one: one supplier order with many lines.

blocks.p: The picture shows the three tables. The order table is on the left, the lines table is in the middle and the part table is on the right. Each line row points back to its order and across to one part. In your own project, the header table keeps the dates, the status and who placed the order. The part number and the quantity move into the lines.

diagram.alt: Three tables drawn as boxes. PartOrder on the left holds PartOrderID, Status and ReceivedOn. PartOrderLine in the middle holds PartOrderLineID, PartOrderID, PartID and QtyOrdered. Part on the right holds PartID, Name and QtyInStock. A line joins PartOrderLine.PartOrderID to PartOrder.PartOrderID, and another joins PartOrderLine.PartID to Part.PartID.
diagram.cap: One order on the left, many lines in the middle. Each line points back to its order and across to one part.

code.title: PartOrderLine and usp_PartOrder_ReceiveLines: an order with many lines
parts: Drop the old lines table first

A line row points at its order, so the lines table is a child of PartOrder. Children are dropped before their parents. In your own script, this line goes at the top of the list of DROP lines, above the order table.
The lines table and its four columns
Each line has its own number, the number of the order it belongs to, the part it is for, and how many were ordered. Three lines of the same order all hold the same PartOrderID.
The key, and the two links

The primary key is the line's own number. The first foreign key links each line to a real order. The second foreign key links each line to a real part, so a line can never be for a part that does not exist.
One line per part, and never zero
UNIQUE on the pair PartOrderID and PartID refuses a second line for the same part on the same order, so 10 inner tubes are one line, not two lines of 5. The CHECK refuses a line for 0 or fewer.
The name, and the one thing that goes in
The stored procedure needs only the order number. Everything else it needs is already in the lines. @Message carries the refusal sentence back out, as in every stored procedure that changes data.
AS, BEGIN and the blank message
AS and BEGIN mark where the work starts. The message starts blank, and a blank message at the end means the delivery was received.
Refuse an order that is not open

An order that has already been received, or was cancelled, must not put the stock up a second time. If there is no open order with this number, the sentence That order is not open. goes back, and RETURN stops the stored procedure there.
Refuse an order with no lines
An order with nothing on it has nothing to receive. The sentence That order has no lines. goes back, and RETURN stops the stored procedure.
The header row is marked Received, with today's date. This is the same UPDATE as in usp_PartOrder_Receive. This version receives every line in full.
Put the stock up for every line at once

This is the line that handles the whole order. The INNER JOIN matches each part to its own line on this order, and each matched part goes up by the quantity on its own line. An order with three lines puts three parts up, in one UPDATE. Parts that are not on the order do not match the join, so they are left as they were. END closes the stored procedure, and GO ends the batch.
code.text:
-- Upgrade 1: one supplier order with many lines.
-- The lines table is a child of PartOrder, so it is dropped first.
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS PartOrderLine;
GO

CREATE TABLE PartOrderLine (
    PartOrderLineID INT IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,
    PartOrderID     INT NOT NULL,
    PartID          INT NOT NULL,
    QtyOrdered      INT NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT PK_PartOrderLine PRIMARY KEY (PartOrderLineID),
    CONSTRAINT FK_PartOrderLine_PartOrder FOREIGN KEY (PartOrderID)
        REFERENCES PartOrder (PartOrderID),
    CONSTRAINT FK_PartOrderLine_Part FOREIGN KEY (PartID)
        REFERENCES Part (PartID),
    -- one line per part on each order
    CONSTRAINT UQ_PartOrderLine UNIQUE (PartOrderID, PartID),
    CONSTRAINT CK_PartOrderLine_Qty CHECK (QtyOrdered > 0)
);
GO

CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE usp_PartOrder_ReceiveLines
    @PartOrderID INT,
    @Message VARCHAR(200) OUTPUT
AS
BEGIN
    SET @Message = '';

    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM PartOrder WHERE PartOrderID = @PartOrderID
        AND Status = 'Ordered')
    BEGIN
        SET @Message = 'That order is not open.';
        RETURN;
    END
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM PartOrderLine
        WHERE PartOrderID = @PartOrderID)
    BEGIN
        SET @Message = 'That order has no lines.';
        RETURN;
    END

    UPDATE PartOrder
    SET Status = 'Received', ReceivedOn = CAST(GETDATE() AS DATE)
    WHERE PartOrderID = @PartOrderID;

    -- Every line at once: each part goes up by its own line's quantity.
    UPDATE Part
    SET QtyInStock = QtyInStock + PartOrderLine.QtyOrdered
    FROM Part
        INNER JOIN PartOrderLine ON PartOrderLine.PartID = Part.PartID
    WHERE PartOrderLine.PartOrderID = @PartOrderID;
END
GO

blocks.p: To place an order with many lines, your own project needs one more stored procedure that adds one line to an open order. Make it by copying usp_PartOrder_Place and moving the part and the quantity into the line table.

stages.title: Upgrade two: a booking held until a deadline

screens.title: Read upgrade two: a booking held for a short time, then let go.

blocks.p: A provisional booking holds its slot like any other booking. The clash check counts every booking that is not cancelled, so nobody else can book that time while it is held. When the deadline passes, the stored procedure usp_Appointment_ExpireProvisional, shown below, cancels the booking and the slot is free again. In your own project, make your diary form, the one you made from frmDiary, run usp_Appointment_ExpireProvisional each time it opens, so a booking that has run out is cancelled before anyone looks.

code.title: A Provisional status, ExpiresOn and usp_Appointment_ExpireProvisional
parts: The word Provisional has eleven letters, and the Status column holds only ten. This line makes it hold twelve. In your own script you type VARCHAR(12) in CREATE TABLE instead, and ALTER TABLE is not needed.
A new column for the deadline
ExpiresOn holds the date and time when the hold runs out. It is empty for an ordinary booking, which never runs out.
Add Provisional to the allowed statuses

The CHECK on the Status column lists the words it allows. The old CHECK is dropped, and a new one is added with Provisional at the front of the list. In your own script, you add the word to the CHECK inside CREATE TABLE.
The name, and the blank message
Nothing goes in, because the stored procedure looks at every held booking. It still has @Message, because it changes data, and the message starts blank.
Cancel every hold whose time is up

Every booking that is Provisional and whose ExpiresOn is before now becomes Cancelled. GETDATE() is the date and time at this moment. The row stays in the table as history, and the time slot is free for someone else. END closes the stored procedure, and GO ends the batch.

blocks.p: To make a provisional booking in your own project, change your copy of usp_Appointment_Add, the stored procedure that adds a booking. Make it set Status to Provisional and ExpiresOn to `DATEADD(HOUR, 48, GETDATE())`, which is 48 hours from now.

To confirm a booking when the deposit is paid, copy usp_Appointment_MarkDone and name the copy usp_Appointment_Confirm. In the copy, change Booked to Provisional in the two places where it looks for the status. Then change the line `SET Status = 'Done'` so that it sets the status to Booked. Last, change the refusal sentence to Only a provisional booking can be confirmed.
